---
title: "Generate Your First Repository"
doc-type: tutorial
---

This tutorial generates a small Downstream Repository, inspects the preview, writes it, and verifies its recorded assets.

## Prerequisites

- A checkout of this Reference Source.
- `uv` available on `PATH`.
- An unused `/tmp/repo-familiar-demo` path.

Install the project environment:

```bash
uv sync
```

## 1. Preview The Repository

Run generation with `--dry-run` first:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate \
  --name "Demo Project" \
  --description "A generated demo." \
  --output /tmp/repo-familiar-demo \
  --template basic \
  --agent-harness opencode \
  --model-profile default-coding \
  --tool-profile cq \
  --skill session-focus \
  --dry-run
```

The preview lists planned files without creating the output directory. Confirm that the selections and paths match the intended repository.

## 2. Generate The Repository

Re-run the same command without `--dry-run`:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate \
  --name "Demo Project" \
  --description "A generated demo." \
  --output /tmp/repo-familiar-demo \
  --template basic \
  --agent-harness opencode \
  --model-profile default-coding \
  --tool-profile cq \
  --skill session-focus
```

The new repository now contains project instructions, selected profile guidance, the selected skill, Quarto docs, a project plan, and `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml` provenance.

## 3. Verify The Result

Check recorded generated assets against their checksums:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar check --path /tmp/repo-familiar-demo
```

The check should report the generated assets as `ok`. Open `/tmp/repo-familiar-demo/.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml` to see the selected template, options, Reference Source identity, and generated-asset records.

- Use [Generate a Repository](../how-to/generate-repository.qmd) for template and profile selection.
- Use [CLI and Metadata Reference](../reference/cli-and-metadata.qmd) for exact command behavior.
- Use [Bootstrap an Existing Repository](../how-to/bootstrap-existing-repository.qmd) instead when the target already contains user-owned files.
